summary: Baij Nath Puri was an Indian scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1950-1952) and served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1971-1976).

Bal Gangadhar Tilak worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Elphinstone College (1873), Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (1873-1877), and Government Law College, Mumbai (1877-1879).

Bal Krishen Thapar was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at the University of the Punjab (~1941-1943). He served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1978-1981).
Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indologist affiliated with Panjab University, where he served as an Assistant (attested 1932) and later as in-charge of the Sanskrit Section (attested 1941).

Bangwei Wang is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. After completing his doctoral dissertation at Peking University (~1984-1987), he became a Professor there, including Professor of Indian and Buddhist Studies (~1993).
Banikanta Kakati was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1913-1918) and served as a professor at Cotton University (~1918-1947).

Barbara E. Ward was a scholar of Sinology who studied at Newnham College (~1937-1940). She held posts at the University of London (~1948-1973), Newnham College (~1973-1983), and the University of Cambridge (~1973-1983).

Barbara Gerke is a scholar of Tibetology who completed a D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held posts at Humboldt University (2011-2015), Oxford (attested 2017), and the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies.
Barbara Nimri Aziz is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She completed her studies at Queen's University (~1958-1962) and SOAS University of London (1969-1974).

Barbara Stoler Miller was an Indologist who studied at Barnard, Columbia, and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD under W. Norman Brown). She served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Studies at Barnard College (~1968-1993).

Barbra R. Clayton works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young (attested 2001) and held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).
Barend Faddegon was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1897-1904) and subsequently held a post there from 1907 to 1944.

Barend Jan Terwiel specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1990-1992), Leiden University (~1992-1993), and the University of Hamburg (~1993-2007).

Barend ter Haar is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and religious studies. After earning his PhD at Leiden University (-1990), he held posts at the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences, Heidelberg University, and Leiden University.

Barry Kerzin works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the Keck School of Medicine of USC (~1972-1976) and UC Berkeley (~1972-1976), and studied under traditional teacher Geshe Namgyal Wangchen.

Barry Sautman works in Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at Columbia University, New York University School of Law, and UCLA School of Law, and held a post at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (~1996).
Bart Dessein specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. A student of Charles Willemen, he served as Associate Professor at Ghent University (attested 2014-2019).
Basil Gould was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Winchester College (~1896-1902) and New College (~1902-1906), and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1906-1947).

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton (~1847-1849) and under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl at the University of Bonn (~1851-1853). He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins University (~1876-1915).

Beata Grant is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning her Ph.D. at Stanford (~1978-1987), she was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley (~1987-1989) and joined Washington University in St. Louis (~1989).
